short: Phidias was a master sculptor and artistic director of the Athenian Acropolis, renowned for his colossal chryselephantine statues.
full:
Active during the 5th century BCE, Phidias was widely regarded as the greatest sculptor of classical Greece. He was a close friend of the statesman Pericles, who appointed him to oversee the massive building programme on the Acropolis following the Persian Wars.

Phidias's most famous works were his monumental statues made of gold and ivory over a wooden core, notably the Athena Parthenos inside the Parthenon and the Statue of Zeus at Olympia, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. While none of his original masterpieces survive, his idealistic, balanced style profoundly defined classical Greek aesthetics and influenced generations of later artists.
